newsitem.title: FINLAND: Benefon says H2 '96 sales weak, no GSM yet.
newsitem.headline: Benefon says H2 '96 sales weak, no GSM yet.

text.p: Finnish mobile phones maker Benefon Oy said in a statement on Friday growth in sales had broken off last autumn and its first GSM product was still waiting for final type approval.

"After the quite weak first months of the year, the sales picked up rapidly in the spring. However, the rapid growth broke off later in the autumn, and the sales of the second half amounted to be only slightly higher than the sales of the first half," it said.
The global cellular market shifted "ever more clearly" to digital services, especially GSM-based services, Benefon said.
The finishing stages of Benefon's first GSM product had "proceeded slower than intended" and the final type approval process could not be finished by the end of 1996, it said.
"Reception of the FTA (final type approval) will be informed separately," it added.
Its 1996 turnover -- 284 million markka or six percent less than 1995 -- came on sales of analog products only, mostly to export markets, Benefon said, adding exports accounted for 94 percent.
"Despite the negative sales growth, the company did not want to cut the present quite heavy expenditure in R&D and in marketing, which are needed for future growth," it said.
Benefon earlier reported a 57 percent fall in preliminary profit after financial items to 32 million markka.
Operating profit fell to 28 million markka from 61 million.
